_help: The Vault Dive (Famous Web3 Hacks). One floor per hack, from the smallest at the top to the biggest at the bottom. amountUsd: approximate US dollars lost, valued at the time of the hack. what: what went wrong, in one or two plain sentences (never how to do it). lesson: how to stay safe. returned: optional note when money came back. Every entry has sources and review: true until checked against them; set review to false once checked.
note: Amounts are approximate, in US dollars at the time of each hack.

hacks.name: Nomad Bridge
hacks.what: A routine upgrade left the bridge accepting withdrawals it should have refused. Once people noticed, hundreds of copycats emptied it within hours.
hacks.lesson: One careless update can open the doors. Bridges hold huge pots of money, so keep only what you need on them.

hacks.name: Euler Finance
hacks.what: A flaw in a newer part of the lending app's code let an attacker take far more than they should have, even though the code had been audited.
hacks.lesson: Audits lower risk, they do not remove it. Do not put everything in one app.
hacks.returned: The attacker returned almost all of it a few weeks later.

hacks.name: WazirX
hacks.what: Attackers got the exchange's wallet signers to approve a change that handed them control of a big wallet. Customer withdrawals were frozen for months.
hacks.lesson: On an exchange, the exchange holds your keys. Keep there only what you are actively trading.

hacks.name: DMM Bitcoin
hacks.what: About 4,500 bitcoin left the Japanese exchange's wallet. The FBI later said North Korean hackers first fooled a worker at its wallet software company.
hacks.lesson: People are the weakest link. Fake job offers and fake files are a favourite way in.

hacks.name: Wormhole
hacks.what: A missing check in the bridge let an attacker create 120,000 wrapped ether that had nothing behind them.
hacks.lesson: A wrapped token is only as good as the bridge behind it.
hacks.returned: Its backer, Jump Crypto, refilled the bridge so users were not left short.

hacks.name: Mt. Gox
hacks.what: The world's biggest bitcoin exchange found about 850,000 bitcoin missing after years of thefts nobody spotted, and collapsed.
hacks.lesson: Not your keys, not your coins. Customers waited about ten years to get some of it back.

hacks.name: FTX
hacks.what: On the very day the exchange filed for bankruptcy, someone drained its wallets. Prosecutors later charged a group that had taken over a staff phone number.
hacks.lesson: When an exchange is in trouble, its security often is too. Move funds you own to your own wallet.

hacks.name: Coincheck
hacks.what: The Japanese exchange kept its NEM coins in a wallet that was always online, and attackers took them in one go.
hacks.lesson: Online hot wallets are handy but risky. Most money should sit in offline cold storage.

hacks.name: BNB Chain bridge
hacks.what: A bug in the bridge's checks let an attacker create 2 million BNB from nothing. The chain was paused and most of it never got out.
hacks.lesson: Some chains can be paused by a small group. That can stop a hack, but it also shows who is really in control.
hacks.returned: Most of it was frozen before it could leave the chain.

hacks.name: Poly Network
hacks.what: A flaw in how the bridge checked who was allowed to move funds let a hacker take them across three chains.
hacks.lesson: Bridges are some of the riskiest places for money in crypto.
hacks.returned: The hacker gave almost all of it back within two weeks.

hacks.name: Ronin Network
hacks.what: Withdrawals needed 5 of 9 keys, and attackers got hold of 5 of them, partly through a fake job offer. Nobody noticed for six days.
hacks.lesson: A few keys means a few targets. Never open files from surprise job offers on a work computer.

hacks.name: Bybit
hacks.what: Attackers tampered with the wallet screen the exchange's signers used, so a transfer that looked routine actually handed over the wallet. It is the biggest crypto theft so far.
hacks.lesson: Check what you are really signing, not just what the screen shows. Hardware wallets help.
